Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — Finova discovery recap

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the proposed next steps so we stay aligned on scope and SLOs. High-level points from our conversation: 

- Primary workload: real-time chat with streaming responses (user-to-bot).
- Latency targets: first-byte streaming p95 <= 300ms; end-to-end completion p95 <= 1.2s for typical 128-token responses.
- Concurrency/throughput: steady-state concurrency target 800 concurrent streams, peak bursts up to 1,200.
- Model profile: production-quality open model (70B quantized or equivalent) with streaming enabled and token-latency-sensitive decoding.
- Availability/operational: reserved capacity with SLA; want predictable reserved throughput for peak trading hours (US market window).

Open questions we captured:
1) Target tokens/sec per stream and average response length — you mentioned ~120 tokens per response average; please confirm.
2) Any hard constraints on non-streaming fallbacks (i.e., if streaming throughput is saturated, is a non-streaming degraded mode acceptable?).
3) Procurement timeline / PO constraints for a 3-month validation trial.

Attached is a draft mutual action plan and a short perf spec spreadsheet (mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf, finova_perf_spec.xlsx) that reflect today's notes.

Recommended immediate next steps:
- Aditya to propose an initial sizing matrix (GPU types and reserved units) and a concrete validation test plan (24-hour steady-state + burst tests).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive next week to walk through the exact hit patterns and metrics we'll collect (trace sampling, token-level latencies).
- Procurement to confirm timeline for a 90-day dedicated validation contract and trial billing cadence.

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update the MAP. Otherwise, I’ll schedule the deep-dive after Aditya sends the sizing notes.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — Finova discovery recap

Thanks Marissa — this looks right from our side. A few clarifications so Aditya can size appropriately: 

- Average response length: 120 tokens (range 40–300). Peak hour avg goes up to ~160 tokens.
- Tokens/sec per stream expectation: we typically see ~30–40 tokens/sec during active generation for our prompt templates.
- KV/cache question: does Redwood persist KV cache for short user sessions (we do session affinity for ~10 minutes); caching latency has big impact on first-token.
- Fallback behavior: streaming is preferred; non-streaming fallback is acceptable for up to 10% of requests during extreme spikes, but we'd like to avoid it if possible.

One more ask: can you share the rough cost delta between A100 vs H100 sizing for the suggested reserved pool? Procurement will need an order-of-magnitude budget.

Appreciate it — Alex

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — Finova discovery recap

Hi Alex — thanks for the details, very helpful. Below are concrete sizing notes and a proposed validation test plan based on the numbers you provided (120–160 tokens, 30–40 tps per stream, steady concurrency 800, peaks to 1,200).

1) Quick answers to questions:
- KV/cache: our Dedicated offering supports in-memory KV cache per instance with session affinity; cache warms are typically <50ms after warm for typical prompts. Persistent cross-instance KV is available as an opt-in (adds small storage/restore overhead) — we can discuss if you need cross-node persistence.
- Non-streaming fallback: configurable policy. We can keep strict streaming-only for SLA-sensitive routes and allow fallback for low-priority routes.

2) GPU comparison (high-level):
- H100 (80GB): best latency and throughput for FP16 + int8 quantized 70B variants. In our internal benchmarks H100 yields ~1.8–2.2x throughput vs A100 on the same model and ~15–25% lower tail latency for streaming workloads.
- A100 (80GB): strong baseline, lower list price in some clouds, but needs ~2x the nodes to match H100 throughput for the same quantized model.
- L4/L40s or smaller cards: cost-effective for lighter models / lower concurrency but will struggle to meet 800 concurrent streaming SLOs on 70B-class models.

3) Recommended reserved pool (starting point for validation):
- Option A (performance-first): 6 x H100 80GB reserved instances. Expected to meet p95 first-byte streaming <= 300ms and end-to-end p95 <= 1.2s for 120–160 token responses under steady 800 concurrency, with headroom for 1.5x bursts.
- Option B (cost-balanced): 12 x A100 80GB reserved instances. Similar end-to-end SLAs but expect slightly higher p95 latency and tighter headroom versus H100.
- Autoscale/burst: We recommend reserving burst capacity (20–50%) as on-demand to handle the +1,200 peak bursts for early validation.

4) Validation test plan (proposal):
- Phase 1 (24-hour steady-state): simulate 800 concurrent streaming sessions at 120 tokens avg, collect token-level latencies, p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, queue lengths.
- Phase 2 (burst tests): 3x 30-minute spike to 1,200 concurrency, observe graceful degradation/fallback behavior.
- Phase 3 (end-to-end correctness): randomized prompt set (200 prompts) to check output parity across model variants and quantization.
- Metrics: first-byte latency, last-byte latency, tokens/sec per GPU, percent requests using fallback, error rates, cost-per-token estimate.

5) Benchmarks and artifacts: attached a quick CSV with representative benchmarking runs (perf-benchmarks-20261103.csv). Note these are examples; we'll run a fuller internal matrix once we lock the model and quantization settings.

Rough cost delta (order of magnitude): H100 reserved nodes ~1.6–2x the per-node cost vs A100 in most cloud price lists, but because you need fewer H100 nodes overall the total reserved spend to achieve the same throughput can be similar or slightly higher depending on provider discounts. We'll push a cost workbook once you confirm cloud/provider preference.

If this looks reasonable I can convert Option A into a concrete reserved SKU list and a 90-day validation quote for procurement (including trial billing terms).

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Great — thanks Aditya and Alex. Summary / agreed next steps:

- Procurement: Finova procurement (procurement@finovalabs.com) to share PO/contract constraints; Marissa will follow up with a draft SOW and the mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf attached.
